html:
Justinian II was Byzantine emperor twice, from 685 to 695 and from 705 to 711, and the last ruler of the Heraclian dynasty. He was the son of Constantine IV and hoped to match the glory of his namesake Justinian I.

In his first reign he called the Quinisext Council, moved Slavs from the Balkans into Anatolia and fought the Umayyads. His harsh tax officials made him hated. In 695 he was overthrown, his nose was cut off so that he could never rule again, and he was exiled to Cherson in Crimea. That began the Twenty Years' Anarchy.

He escaped, married a sister of the Khazar khagan, and won the help of the Bulgar ruler Tervel. In 705 he got into Constantinople through an aqueduct and took the throne back. Some accounts say he wore a nose of gold. His second reign was a run of revenge killings. In 711 he was overthrown again and killed, and his young son was murdered too.
sum: Justinian II was Byzantine emperor twice, from 685 to 695 and from 705 to 711, and the last ruler of the Heraclian dynasty. He was the son of Constantine IV and hoped to match the glory of his namesake Justinian I.
